key_insight: Lung-R1 uses a pulmonary knowledge graph to turn general LLM knowledge into patient-specific, relation-aware diagnostic reasoning from EMR evidence.
clinical_relevance: This could improve pulmonary diagnostic support by helping models integrate heterogeneous records more reliably than simple knowledge recall.
method: Built LungKG, a structured pulmonary knowledge graph with 59,038 nodes, 164,308 edges, 15 entity types, and 112 relation types.
Trained Lung-R1 with KG-constrained reasoning-chain construction and KG-guided reinforcement learning.
Designed the system for record-grounded pulmonary diagnosis and evaluation across QA and EMR tasks.
evidence_signal: In a 20-system evaluation, Lung-R1-14B achieved state-of-the-art results and scored 4.3583 on EMR Diagnosis, exceeding the strongest non-Lung-R1 baseline by 0.1476 points.
watch_item: Performance gains from a specialized knowledge graph may not directly generalize across institutions, documentation styles, or broader clinical settings without further validation.
paper_title: Lung-R1: A Knowledge Graph-Guided LLM for Pulmonary Diagnostic Reasoning
